 University of Oklahoma officials announced special promotions for fans after Saturday’s planned game against Ole Miss was shifted to Sunday in a last-minute decision.
 Updated: 11:01 PM CST Nov 14, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Josh Wallace Digital Editor NORMAN, Okla. — University of Oklahoma officials on Saturday announced special promotions for fans after Saturday’s planned game against Ole Miss was shifted to Sunday in a last-minute decision. 
 Fans coming to Gaylord Family Oklahoma Memorial Stadium will receive reduced concession prices, with items such as hotdogs, soft drinks, hot chocolate and select beers, available for $2.
 Advertisement Fans will also receive free hand warmers and ponchos at the Sooner Shop, west of the stadium, while supplies last.
 Merchandise will also be discounted, with an automatic 20 percent off merchandise storewide and 60 percent off select items at the Sooner Shop.
 SEC told OU not playing Ole Miss on Sunday 'would result in a forfeit,' Oklahoma AD says University officials also said students will receive free attendance to the game and do not need to show a game ticket. Students must show a valid OU student I.D. at the Gate 7 student entrance, and all students will receive a wristband upon entry, according to a news release.
 'Absolutely wrong': Bob Stoops calls out SEC's decision to postpone OU-Ole Miss game to Sunday Officials also announced special ticket offers, which include complimentary tickets for upcoming OU events, such as the Dec. 1 men’s basketball game against Syracuse. Officials said more events would be announced next week.
